title: ERP Stakeholder Interview: Questions, What They Map To, and What They Produce

questions.question: Tell me about your current role on your project. What are the main things you produce, decide or review in a typical week?
questions.deliverable: Every deliverable (all findings split by persona); learning pathways by work performed
questions.notes: Confirm the role from the profile form. Which of those tasks involve writing up meetings, designs, plans, status or test material?

questions.question: Think of a typical week. Where does time go on work that isn't advising the client or making decisions, such as writing up meetings, drafting requirements or designs, building plans and reports, or chasing status?
questions.laterAgents: Requirements capture; Functional and technical design drafts; Status reports; Delivery plans
questions.deliverable: Impact assessment; adoption measurement approach and 30/60/90-day reports
questions.notes: Roughly how many hours a week on each? Which would you most like back?

questions.question: What had you heard before today, and from whom? What is unclear or sounds like jargon?
questions.deliverable: Change vision; communications plan and collateral; FAQs
questions.notes: Show: What to expect (slide 3) and the roadmap (slide 5). What had you heard before today, and from whom? What is unclear or sounds like jargon?

questions.question: Which agents from wave 1 are the most/least useful for your role? Waves 2-4?
questions.deliverable: Persona-specific messages; learning pathways; plans for later releases
questions.notes: Show: agent glossary (slide 6). Record ratings in the Agent Heat Map tab. Is anything missing? If an agent matters mainly in a later wave, what makes it matter?

questions.question: If this works as planned, what gets better for you in your day-to-day, first with the agents arriving by end of December and then as later agents arrive? What would make it worth the effort of changing how you work?
questions.wave1Agents: Meeting recaps; Knowledge hub; Attention dashboard
questions.laterAgents: Requirements capture; Status reports; Delivery plans
questions.deliverable: Vision and messaging; launch message; persona-specific communications
questions.notes: What would you tell a colleague in your role is in it for them?

questions.question: When an agent flags something for you, such as two documents that disagree, an out-of-date document, a risk in a design draft or a concern that keeps coming up, who should be told, how would you like to hear (Teams, email, ADO, a personal to-do list), and what would make you start ignoring these alerts?
questions.laterAgents: Functional design drafts (risk flags for the architect)
questions.deliverable: Communications plan; input to agent design
questions.notes: Which channels do you already check daily?

questions.question: Even if the agents work well, what would stop you using them in your normal delivery, now and as more agents arrive?
questions.laterAgents: Agents that draft work: requirements, designs, test cases, plans, status reports
questions.deliverable: Risks and mitigations in the change and adoption plan; PM/OL review
questions.notes: Does your answer change for agents that draft documents compared with agents that only watch and flag? Time, trust, permissions, client concerns, habit?

questions.question: What would you need to see to trust an agent's output, and what could we show you before December? Would you need more proof for agents that draft requirements, designs or test cases?
questions.wave1Agents: Meeting recaps; Continuous checks; Knowledge hub
questions.laterAgents: Requirements capture; Fit-gap sorting; Design drafts; Test cases
questions.deliverable: Engagement and communications plan (demos, early adopters)
questions.notes: A live demo, a colleague using it, accuracy results? Whose use of it would carry the most weight?

questions.question: Based on the work you do on a project, what would you need to learn or practice to use these agents well, both the first five and the ones that draft requirements, designs, plans or reports later?
questions.laterAgents: Requirements capture; Design drafts; Delivery plans; Status reports; Training content
questions.deliverable: Learning pathways and learning journey with L&D
questions.notes: Which tasks would you want help with first? What would you want explained in the terms of your own work (finance, supply chain, technical, delivery management)? How would you check an agent's draft?

questions.question: The plan includes a short online course, half-day sessions, office hours, a peer community and coaching. Which would you use, and for later agents would you want training as each one arrives or ahead of time?
questions.laterAgents: Each later agent as it arrives; Training content
questions.deliverable: Learning journey; training plan; engagement plan
questions.notes: What would make you attend rather than postpone?

questions.question: How do you usually hear about practice-wide changes (channel, sender), which of those do you actually read or act on, and how often would you want updates as later agents get dates?
questions.laterAgents: All later waves (updates as dates firm up)
questions.deliverable: Communications plan; weekly Teams posts; FAQs
questions.notes: Which message did you most recently act on, and why?

questions.question: Whose view would most influence whether you try a new way of working?
questions.notes: Role or named people. Would they be supportive? Who else should we talk to?

questions.question: Would you want to help test or champion the agents arriving by end of December, or help shape a later agent in your area, such as requirements, design, plans or status? What would you need in order to say yes?
questions.laterAgents: Early input on a later agent in their area
questions.deliverable: Engagement plan; Wave 1 testing; later-release planning
questions.notes: How much time could you give? Would recognition for early adopters matter, and in what form?

questions.question: A few months after rollout, how would you know it is working, for you and for your team? What would you notice, and what should we measure as later agents arrive?
questions.laterAgents: Later agents' measures as they land
questions.notes: Usage, time saved, quality, fewer late surprises, satisfaction?

questions.question: What is the one thing we should do, or avoid, to make this work, for the first agents and for what comes after?
questions.deliverable: Risks in the change and adoption plan; leadership-ready summary page
